passages.note: Direct quotations attributed to Sen. Greg Taylor, D-Indianapolis criticizing the camping-ban bill's 300-foot clause and its $500 fine, with no enforcement rule of his own named.

rows.reasoning: Taylor's quoted remarks oppose this bill's penalties: he asks "Why would you prescribe any distance away?", says "What I think we should be working on is finding a place for the unhoused to be housed", and calls a $500 fine on an impoverished homeless person "dangerous". That establishes a side but no rung: nothing in his words chooses between "Protecting the right to sleep and shelter in public spaces, with no penalties of any kind", "Decriminalizing public sleeping and camping in public spaces", and "Allowing enforcement only when adequate shelter beds are available, with citations diverting people to services rather than the criminal justice system". The article reports no act of his on the bill, so there is no record to code.

Taylor's own words naming the enforcement rule he would adopt (floor statement, questionnaire, or issue page), rather than his objections to this bill

quotes.text: What I think we should be working on is finding a place for the unhoused to be housed. This is a bill that looks for a place for the unhoused to remain unhoused, because you can actually move 300 feet and not violate this law.
